core_claim.quote: The core claim from the perspective of consciousness is that conscious contents are given by the brain’s ‘best guesses’ – by the joint content of the top-down perceptual predictions

source.citation: Seth AK. Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism. Behavioral and Brain Sciences 49, e315 (published online 2025-04-21)

prediction.statement: What a person expects shapes what they consciously perceive: an expected stimulus becomes conscious sooner than an unexpected one, and by the same reasoning an expected signal from inside the body is felt earlier than an unexpected one.

first_stated.passage: In the visual domain, expectations about upcoming sensory input reduce the latency of neuronal signatures differentiating seen and unseen stimuli (Melloni et al., 2011); in other words, expectations speed up conscious access. By analogy, an expected interoceptive signal may be perceived as occurring earlier than an unexpected interoceptive signal.

source.citation: Seth AK, Suzuki K, Critchley HD. An interoceptive predictive coding model of conscious presence. Frontiers in Psychology 2:395 (2011 volume)

prediction.test_for: Stimuli the person was led to expect are reported, or show the brain's seen-versus-unseen difference, earlier than the same stimuli unexpected; or a heartbeat-timed signal that is expected is judged earlier than one that is not.
prediction.test_against: With expectation manipulated and the stimuli physically the same, expected stimuli become conscious no sooner (or later) than unexpected ones.
